column12: Eligible randomized, double-blind, four-arm perioperative trial of needle-free surface electroacupuncture (Silver Spike Point, SSP) versus sham SSP and general-anesthesia-only control in women undergoing hysterectomy. Complete attached 7-page PDF reviewed, including Tables 1-8, Figures 1-3, footnotes, and acknowledgments; no supplement is cited or attached. Randomized n=49: Group 1 control n=13, Group 2 sham n=12, Group 3 100-Hz SSP n=12, Group 4 low-frequency dense-sparse SSP n=12. Two Group 4 participants discontinued because they could not carry out VAS; analyzed n=47 (13/12/12/10). All groups received postoperative IV morphine PCA: after one hour in recovery, 0.8-mg boluses for the subsequent 23 hours, 8-minute lockout (PDF p. 3, sec. 2.3). Table 8 reports cumulative 24-hour morphine delivered (mean±SD, mg): 38.63±11.08, 34.20±6.40, 31.14±8.15, 29.29±8.89 for Groups 1-4, respectively. Pain VAS 0-10 was reported at 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 8, 16, and 24 hours, but the activity condition (rest/movement) was not stated; keep as activity unspecified. No values were converted or inferred. Additional exact outcomes (arm order: control, sham SSP, 100-Hz SSP, dense-sparse 3/10/20-Hz SSP): first bowel movement, mean±SD hours, 37.54±2.93, 38.03±2.71, 35.50±2.64, 33.30±2.43 (Table 3, PDF p. 2); first ambulation, mean±SD hours, 32.50±2.41, 33.75±3.11, 33.13±3.18, 29.90±2.95 (Table 4, PDF p. 3). Total 24-hour PCA deliveries, mean±SD counts, 29.16±11.79, 31.82±11.98, 27.75±11.78, 23.30±11.93; total 24-hour PCA demands, mean±SD counts, 84.54±38.66, 74.18±39.33, 52.17±21.87, 41.60±36.47 (Table 8, PDF p. 5). Interval morphine delivered (mg) is reported in Table 6, but interval means do not arithmetically reproduce the separate Table 8 cumulative means; no reconciliation was inferred and independent verification is required. SSP side effects (bruising, dizziness, anxiety) and opioid-related effects were assessed, but no arm-level numerical results are reported.

column12: Eligible pilot prospective randomized double-blind sham-controlled trial of postoperative electroacupuncture after open thoracotomy for operable non-small-cell lung cancer. Twenty-seven randomized; two excluded after randomization for unrelated complications (respiratory failure requiring ventilation; gastrointestinal bleeding requiring endoscopy); 25 analyzed: EA 13, sham 12. EA used ipsilateral LI4, GB34, GB36, and TE8 with penetrating needles, de qi, 60-Hz alternating current for 30 min twice daily from ward return through postoperative day 7. Sham used blunt nonpenetrating needles at the same acupoints, opaque fixators, and an incorrectly connected device with no current. Both arms received IV PCA morphine 1 mg/bolus, 5-min lockout for postoperative days 0–2 plus oral acetaminophen 640 mg/dextropropoxyphene 65 mg four times daily. Exact PCA morphine values (Table 2, PDF p.2034), EA vs sham: day 0 8.3±4.9 vs 7.8±6.4 mg; day 1 18.0±8.8 vs 18.8±9.8 mg; day 2 7.5±5.0 vs 15.7±12.0 mg; total through day 2 33.9±12.8 vs 42.3±21.3 mg. These are postoperative calendar-day intervals, not a clearly identifiable cumulative 0–24 h value. VAS 0–10, activity condition unspecified, day 0 through day 7: EA 3.7±1.6, 3.9±1.3, 3.1±1.4, 2.9±1.1, 3.0±1.5, 2.5±1.8, 3.2±1.9, 3.0±3.6; sham 3.0±2.3, 3.9±1.4, 3.8±1.6, 3.8±1.9, 4.4±1.9, 4.0±1.1, 4.8±2.1, 3.0±1.4 (Table 2, p.2034). No acupuncture-related mortality, complications, infection, bleeding, or other adverse reactions were reported. column12:
Eligible randomized three-arm perioperative electroacupuncture trial in 90 women (30/arm) undergoing elective total abdominal hysterectomy ± bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy; all 90 analyzed, no withdrawals reported. Full 10-page PDF, Tables 1–2, Figures 1–4 and footnotes checked.

Actual arms (locked two-column form cannot represent all three):
Group I control: placebo EA for 45 min preoperatively; plastic tube tapped near bilateral ST36/PC6 and incision sites, needles taped without skin penetration, mock stimulator indicator light, no current.
Group II preoperative EA: bilateral ST36 and PC6 plus subcutaneous needling along incision; 45 min before GA, with incision-site stimulation continuing until end of surgery. 2 Hz at ST36/PC6 and 100 Hz at incision; WQ1002K AERON Beijing; ST36 depth 3–4 cm, PC6 0.5–1 cm, 0.25-mm needles.
Group III postoperative EA: same active EA regimen for 45 min on arrival in recovery after extubation/awakening. PDF pp. 2–3.

Common co-interventions: balanced GA with protocolized alfentanil; IV morphine 0.1 mg/kg after alfentanil, then 1–2 mg every 5 min in recovery until VAS ≤3, followed by PCA morphine 1 mg demand/5-min lockout; ondansetron 4 mg IV. PDF pp. 2–3.

Exact results (Group I / II / III):
Cumulative postoperative morphine 0–24 h, mean±SD: 0.68±0.38 / 0.52±0.19 / 0.58±0.27 mg/kg (n=30 each), PDF p. 4 and Fig 4 p. 6.
Morphine 6–12 h, median (IQR), not mean/SD: 0.10 (0.11) / 0.03 (0.05) / 0.08 (0.10) mg/kg, PDF p. 4.
Other 6-h intervals are graph-only in Fig 3; no values inferred.
Intraoperative alfentanil, mean±SD: 0.51±0.21 / 0.44±0.15 / 0.58±0.22 µg/kg/min, Table 1 p. 4.
Pain at rest, mean across the 24-h assessment period (not a 24-h point estimate), 0–10 VAS mean±SD: 4.5±2.1 / 4.7±1.8 / 3.9±1.6, Table 2 p. 5. Separate 6-hour timepoint values were not tabulated.
PONV incidence reported only as percentages: 46.6% / 43.3% / 56.7%; drowsiness 30.0% / 23.3% / 33.3%; pruritus 16.7% / 13.3% / 16.7%. Counts were not reported and were not derived. Table 2 p. 5.
No EA-related complications reported; 65% of EA recipients said they would accept EA again. PDF p. 6.

Do not complete: only first reviewer can set up interventions/outcomes, and the present two-arm structure conflates the two active timing arms and omits one actual study arm.

Eligible randomized three-arm perioperative electroacupuncture trial in 90 women (30/arm) undergoing elective total abdominal hysterectomy ± bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy; all 90 analyzed, no withdrawals reported. Full 10-page PDF, Tables 1–2, Figures 1–4 and footnotes checked.

Actual arms (locked two-column form cannot represent all three):
Group I control: placebo EA for 45 min preoperatively; plastic tube tapped near bilateral ST36/PC6 and incision sites, needles taped without skin penetration, mock stimulator indicator light, no current.
Group II preoperative EA: bilateral ST36 and PC6 plus subcutaneous needling along incision; 45 min before GA, with incision-site stimulation continuing until end of surgery. 2 Hz at ST36/PC6 and 100 Hz at incision; WQ1002K AERON Beijing; ST36 depth 3–4 cm, PC6 0.5–1 cm, 0.25-mm needles.
Group III postoperative EA: same active EA regimen for 45 min on arrival in recovery after extubation/awakening. PDF pp. 2–3.

Common co-interventions: balanced GA with protocolized alfentanil; IV morphine 0.1 mg/kg after alfentanil, then 1–2 mg every 5 min in recovery until VAS ≤3, followed by PCA morphine 1 mg demand/5-min lockout; ondansetron 4 mg IV. PDF pp. 2–3.

Exact results (Group I / II / III):
Cumulative postoperative morphine 0–24 h, mean±SD: 0.68±0.38 / 0.52±0.19 / 0.58±0.27 mg/kg (n=30 each), PDF p. 4 and Fig 4 p. 6.
Morphine 6–12 h, median (IQR), not mean/SD: 0.10 (0.11) / 0.03 (0.05) / 0.08 (0.10) mg/kg, PDF p. 4.
Other 6-h intervals are graph-only in Fig 3; no values inferred.
Intraoperative alfentanil, mean±SD: 0.51±0.21 / 0.44±0.15 / 0.58±0.22 µg/kg/min, Table 1 p. 4.
Pain at rest, mean across the 24-h assessment period (not a 24-h point estimate), 0–10 VAS mean±SD: 4.5±2.1 / 4.7±1.8 / 3.9±1.6, Table 2 p. 5. Separate 6-hour timepoint values were not tabulated.
PONV incidence reported only as percentages: 46.6% / 43.3% / 56.7%; drowsiness 30.0% / 23.3% / 33.3%; pruritus 16.7% / 13.3% / 16.7%. Counts were not reported and were not derived. Table 2 p. 5.
No EA-related complications reported; 65% of EA recipients said they would accept EA again. PDF p. 6.

column9: Project of National Clinical Research Base of Traditional Chinese Medicine in Jiangsu Province, China
column11: Jiangsu Province Hospital of Chinese Medicine (Affiliated Hospital of Nanjing University of Traditional Chinese Medicine), China; March–August 2017. PDF p. 2.
column12:
Eligible three-arm, single-blind randomized trial of postoperative TEAS added to bilateral transverse abdominis plane (TAP) block after elective open abdominal surgery. Full six-page PDF, CONSORT flow, Tables 1–4 and footnotes checked. Ninety-one enrolled; one withdrew for personal reasons before the final randomized cohort; 90 randomized 1:1:1 and all completed (30/arm). Exact allocation timing relative to the one withdrawal is described inconsistently; Results says after randomization all patients completed.

Actual arms (locked two-column form cannot represent all three):
1) TAP group: bilateral ultrasound-guided TAP blocks at end of surgery, 20 mL 0.375% ropivacaine each side, plus common PCIA.
2) TAP + TEAS group: same TAP block plus TEAS at bilateral ST36 and PC6 for 30 min before leaving PACU and again at 24 h; KD2B stimulator, sparse-dense wave 2–100 Hz, intensity increased from zero to strong but comfortable; electrode details/current amplitude not reported.
3) Usual care group: PCIA only, with no TAP block and no TEAS.
All arms: PCIA solution 100 µg sufentanil + 6 mg tropisetron in 100 mL, basal infusion 2 mL/h for 48 h. No PCA demand-dose/lockout stated. PDF pp. 2–3.

No postoperative opioid consumption, delivered PCA volume, bolus count, rescue-analgesia count, or 0–24 h opioid dose was measured/reported; do not infer consumption from the fixed solution or basal rate.

Pain activity condition unspecified; 100-mm VAS at 2, 24, 48 h. Table 2 notation is undefined and must be preserved verbatim (nonparametric analysis; neither mean/SD nor median/IQR is identified):
TAP / TAP+TEAS / usual care:
2 h: 2(1.7 ± 3.0) / 2(2.0 ± 3.0) / 2(2.0 ± 3.0)
24 h: 2(2.0 ± 3.0) / 2(1.7 ± 2.2) / 3(2.0 ± 4.0)
48 h: 2(2.0 ± 3.0) / 2(1.7 ± 2.0) / 3(2.0 ± 3.2)
PDF p. 4, Table 2. Do not enter these as mean/SD without author clarification.

Adverse events, count/30:
Dizziness at 24/48/72 h: TAP 10/5/2; TAP+TEAS 2/0/0; usual care 14/8/3.
Composite nausea/vomiting at 24/48/72 h: TAP 8/6/3; TAP+TEAS 3/1/0; usual care 13/12/8.
Total adverse-event cases at 24/48/72 h: TAP 12/8/3; TAP+TEAS 4/1/0; usual care 18/13/8. These totals are not necessarily unique participants across categories/timepoints. No other adverse reactions found. PDF p. 5, Table 4.

column9: Project of National Clinical Research Base of Traditional Chinese Medicine in Jiangsu Province, China
column11: Jiangsu Province Hospital of Chinese Medicine (Affiliated Hospital of Nanjing University of Traditional Chinese Medicine), China; March–August 2017. PDF p. 2.
column12:
Eligible three-arm, single-blind randomized trial of postoperative TEAS added to bilateral transverse abdominis plane (TAP) block after elective open abdominal surgery. Full six-page PDF, CONSORT flow, Tables 1–4 and footnotes checked. Ninety-one enrolled; one withdrew for personal reasons before the final randomized cohort; 90 randomized 1:1:1 and all completed (30/arm). Exact allocation timing relative to the one withdrawal is described inconsistently; Results says after randomization all patients completed.

Actual arms (locked two-column form cannot represent all three):
1) TAP group: bilateral ultrasound-guided TAP blocks at end of surgery, 20 mL 0.375% ropivacaine each side, plus common PCIA.
2) TAP + TEAS group: same TAP block plus TEAS at bilateral ST36 and PC6 for 30 min before leaving PACU and again at 24 h; KD2B stimulator, sparse-dense wave 2–100 Hz, intensity increased from zero to strong but comfortable; electrode details/current amplitude not reported.
3) Usual care group: PCIA only, with no TAP block and no TEAS.
All arms: PCIA solution 100 µg sufentanil + 6 mg tropisetron in 100 mL, basal infusion 2 mL/h for 48 h. No PCA demand-dose/lockout stated. PDF pp. 2–3.

No postoperative opioid consumption, delivered PCA volume, bolus count, rescue-analgesia count, or 0–24 h opioid dose was measured/reported; do not infer consumption from the fixed solution or basal rate.

Pain activity condition unspecified; 100-mm VAS at 2, 24, 48 h. Table 2 notation is undefined and must be preserved verbatim (nonparametric analysis; neither mean/SD nor median/IQR is identified):

2 h: 2(1.7 ± 3.0) / 2(2.0 ± 3.0) / 2(2.0 ± 3.0)
24 h: 2(2.0 ± 3.0) / 2(1.7 ± 2.2) / 3(2.0 ± 4.0)
48 h: 2(2.0 ± 3.0) / 2(1.7 ± 2.0) / 3(2.0 ± 3.2)
PDF p. 4, Table 2. Do not enter these as mean/SD without author clarification.

Adverse events, count/30:
Dizziness at 24/48/72 h: TAP 10/5/2; TAP+TEAS 2/0/0; usual care 14/8/3.
Composite nausea/vomiting at 24/48/72 h: TAP 8/6/3; TAP+TEAS 3/1/0; usual care 13/12/8.
Total adverse-event cases at 24/48/72 h: TAP 12/8/3; TAP+TEAS 4/1/0; usual care 18/13/8. These totals are not necessarily unique participants across categories/timepoints. No other adverse reactions found. PDF p. 5, Table 4.
